spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 587.56 nm (the d line). The publication's index column is headed Ne, but the index pairs it carries (1.883 / 40.7645, 1.603 / 65.4427) are d-line values, so the record is evaluated at the d line. Converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values are for display only

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

effective_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

comparison.why: the publication states neither an effective focal length nor a back focal length for this example, so the two-quantity rule has no pair to judge. The engine's values are recorded under engine_check as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts and no verdict is claimed

field.note: the publication's parameter table states an F-number, a half angle of view and an image height per example, but this batch did not confirm which row belongs to this table, so no field value is asserted

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated Nd. A patent table gives Nd and vd only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material.

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the stated Abbe number is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled
the Project is evaluated at the d line only

the source states no clear apertures; semi-diameters were derived from the axial marginal beam (0.08 mm at the stated F-number) with clearance for the 15 mm conjugate's off-axis beam, growing 0.45 mm to 0.60 mm toward the image. They set the stop plate and the solid checks, not the first-order values
the source's object row states a distance of 15 without naming the unit or confirming it as the object distance; it is read as 15 mm, the unit the rest of the table uses
the source gives no stop-plate outer radius; the plate reaches the largest clear semi-diameter beside the stop
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled
